haiku-low.q1: A message on the domain-events topic; the Dispatcher consumes it and creates delivery rows. Who produces that message is NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q2: Dispatcher inserts one row per active subscription matching the account and event_type or '*', in one transaction, with unique (event_id, subscription_id) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, so a redelivered message is a no-op.
haiku-low.q3: The signature covers 't.<raw body>' via HMAC-SHA256 with the secret, where t is now. It is produced again on each attempt.
haiku-low.q4: 2xx: delivered. 410: disable subscription and dead-letter this row and its pending rows. Other 4xx: dead. 408, 429, 5xx, timeout, connection error: retry until attempt 8, then dead.
haiku-low.q5: At most 8 attempts. The third attempt is made 2 minutes after the second attempt fails.
haiku-low.q6: In the deliveries table in the service's own Postgres: status, attempt, next_attempt_at, last_status_code and last_error columns.
haiku-low.q7: It waits in the deliveries table with next_attempt_at set. Workers poll Postgres about every 1 s and claim due rows with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED.
haiku-low.q8: After the 30 s lease expires, any worker reclaims the row and may send it again, so a duplicate is possible. The reclaim counts as an attempt; if the crashed one was the 8th, it is dead-lettered.
haiku-low.q9: Dead rows stay in the deliveries table with status dead. Replay sets status pending, attempt 0, next_attempt_at now, clears dead_at, keeping the same delivery id.
haiku-low.q10: The X-Webhook-Id header carries the delivery id. It never changes between retries or after a replay.
haiku-low.q11: Waiting rows are dead-lettered with last_error 'subscription disabled'. They are not sent and not silently dropped; workers check at claim time.

sonnet.q1: A message on the `domain-events` topic (the queue) starts it; the dispatcher consumes it. Which existing component publishes to that topic is NOT STATED.
sonnet.q2: The dispatcher reads the active subscriptions for the event's account_id whose event_types contain the event_type or '*'. It inserts one deliveries row per subscription in one transaction. The unique (event_id, subscription_id) key with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING makes a redelivered message's insert a no-op. The ack comes after the commit.
sonnet.q3: The signature covers "<t>.<raw body>" (timestamp, a dot, then the raw body), using HMAC-SHA256 with the subscription secret. It is produced again on every attempt, with t = now.
sonnet.q4: 2xx: status delivered. 410: disable the subscription (reason 'gone') and dead-letter this row and all its pending rows. Other 4xx: dead immediately. 408, 429, 5xx, timeout and connection error: retry if attempt < 8 (status pending, next_attempt_at = now + wait), otherwise dead.
sonnet.q5: At most 8 attempts per cycle. The third attempt is made 2 minutes after the second fails.
sonnet.q6: In the single `deliveries` table in the service's own Postgres. The columns are status, attempt, next_attempt_at, and last_status_code and last_error.
sonnet.q7: It waits in the deliveries table as a pending row with next_attempt_at set to a future time. Workers poll Postgres about every 1 s and claim rows that are due (pending AND next_attempt_at <= now), so the queue is not used.
sonnet.q8: The row stays in_flight with a 30 s lease. When the lease expires, any worker reclaims it and the delivery may be sent twice (at-least-once). The reclaim counts as an attempt, and if that crashed attempt was the 8th, the row is dead-lettered instead of sent. No row is lost.
sonnet.q9: They are held in the same deliveries table with status = dead. A replay sets status to pending, attempt to 0 and next_attempt_at to now, and clears dead_at. The delivery id is kept, and the row gets a fresh cycle of 8 attempts.
sonnet.q10: The delivery id, sent as the X-Webhook-Id header. It never changes, not between retries and not on replay.
sonnet.q11: They are dead-lettered, not sent and not silently dropped, with last_error = 'subscription disabled'. Workers check this at claim time, and a 410 dead-letters the pending rows immediately. Support can replay them after the customer re-enables the subscription. A replay is rejected while the subscription is still disabled.
sonnet.q12: NOT STATED. The document gives no ordering guarantee. It does say retries wait up to 6 hours while rows are claimed independently by several workers.
